requirements.statement: Every category in a label is one of the 39 categories of the taxonomy, written exactly as the taxonomy writes it.

source: bad.push({start: mm.index, end: mm.index + x.length, why: 'category not in taxonomy form: ' + c});

means: Checks each category name in the label has the Family – form the taxonomy uses; the full list of 39 is not in the material, so only the form is checked.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a timecode span, start–end in mm:ss, inside the clip's duration.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s = (+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e = (+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (e <= s) bad.push({start:m.index, end:m.index+m[0].length, why:'end not after start'}); } const d = text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); if (d) { const dur = (+d[1])*60+(+d[2]); const re2 = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; while ((m = re2.exec(text))) { const e = (+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (e > dur) bad.push({start:m.index, end:m.index+m[0].length, why:'span runs past duration'}); } } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' span problem(s)' : 'spans inside duration', spans: bad }; }
means: Each span is read as mm:ss start and end; the end must be after the start and inside the clip duration.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a risk level: Low, Medium or High.

return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' missing or invalid risk' : 'risk levels valid', spans: bad };

requirements.statement: "High" risk requires an explicit depiction in the clip: a described act, injury, blood, a weapon fired, an explicit sexual act. A reference, a mention or a discussion is Medium at most.
A clip labelled "Firearms – depiction" or "Firearms – use" is never also labelled "Floor – all brands".

source: (text) => { const hasFirearm = /Firearms – (depiction|use)/.test(text); const hasFloor = /Floor – all brands/.test(text); const ok = !(hasFirearm && hasFloor); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'no firearm and floor label together' : 'firearm label with Floor – all brands', spans: ok ? [] : [{start: text.indexOf('Floor – all brands'), end: text.indexOf('Floor – all brands')+18, why:'Floor label alongside firearm label'}] }; }
means: Checks that a firearm category and the Floor label do not both appear in the label.

requirements.statement: A clip with no flagged category is labelled "Floor – all brands" with risk Floor and no timecode.

source: (text) => { const hasFloor = /"Floor – all brands"/.test(text); const cats = (text.match(/"category"\s*:/g) || []).length; if (cats === 0) { const ok = /"risk"\s*:\s*"Floor"/.test(text) && !/"span"/.test(text); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'no-flag label correct' : 'no-flag label missing Floor risk or has timecode', spans: [] }; } return { ok: true, detail: 'clip has flagged categories; rule does not apply', spans: [] }; }
means: If the label holds no categories, it must carry risk Floor and no span. Otherwise the rule does not apply.

bad.push({ start: 0, end: 0, why: 'category ' + i + ' has no evidence' });

requirements.statement: "Violence – graphic" requires described injury or blood; a scuffle, a push or a threat is "Violence – minor".
"Language – strong" requires a word of the strong list in the transcript; "Language – mild" otherwise.
A label carries no category the transcript does not support with evidence.
Risk is the highest of the flagged categories' risk levels, carried once at the top of the label as overall.

source: (text) => { const order = {Floor:0, Low:1, Medium:2, High:3}; const o = text.match(/"overall"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/); const risks = [...text.matchAll(/"risk"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g)].map(x=>x[1]); if (!o) return { ok:false, detail:'no overall', spans:[] }; if (risks.length === 0) return { ok: o[1]==='Floor', detail:'overall with no categories', spans:[] }; const top = risks.reduce((a,b)=> (order[b]??0) > (order[a]??0) ? b : a); const ok = o[1] === top; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'overall equals highest risk' : 'overall should be ' + top, spans: ok ? [] : [{start:o.index, end:o.index+o[0].length, why:'overall not highest risk'}] }; }
means: The overall value must equal the highest risk among the categories.

requirements.statement: A span's end is after its start, and no span runs past the duration.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const d = text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); const dur = d ? (+d[1])*60+(+d[2]) : null; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s=(+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e=(+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (e<=s) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'end not after start'}); else if (dur!==null && e>dur) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'runs past duration'}); } return { ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length+' span(s) invalid' : 'spans ordered and within duration', spans: bad }; }
means: Each span's end is after its start and does not exceed the clip duration.

requirements.statement: Where the same act is both "Violence" and "Dangerous acts", both are flagged, each with its own evidence.
A news report of a disaster is "Disaster – news", Medium at most; graphic footage described is "Disaster – graphic".
A reference to alcohol in passing is "Alcohol – reference", Low; drinking described is "Alcohol – consumption", Medium.
Numbers in a span are seconds and minutes only: no frame counts.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { if (/frame/i.test(m[1]) || /\d+\s*f\b/.test(m[1])) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'frame count in span'}); } return { ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length ? 'frame count found in span' : 'no frame counts in spans', spans: bad }; }

requirements.statement: Evidence is copied from the transcript, never paraphrased.

source: if (ev.length && !isPlaceholder && !T.includes(ev)) bad.push({start: m.index, end: m.index+m[0].length, why: 'evidence not found verbatim in transcript'});
return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' evidence quote(s) not verbatim' : 'all evidence verbatim', spans: bad };
means: Each evidence string must appear word for word in the material (case and spacing aside).

requirements.statement: A category flagged twice is listed once, with the earliest span.

source: (text) => { const cats = [...text.matchAll(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g)].map(x=>x[1]); const seen = new Set(); const bad = []; for (const c of cats) { if (seen.has(c)) bad.push({start:text.indexOf('"'+c+'"'), end:text.indexOf('"'+c+'"')+c.length+2, why:'category listed more than once'}); seen.add(c); } return { ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length+' duplicate category(ies)' : 'each category listed once', spans: bad }; }
means: No category name appears twice in the categories list. Choice of earliest span is not checked.

requirements.statement: The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.

source: (text) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return { ok:false, detail:'not valid JSON', spans:[] }; } const keys = Object.keys(obj).sort().join(','); const ok = keys === 'categories,clip,duration,overall'; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'JSON with exact keys' : 'keys are ' + keys, spans: [] }; }
means: The label parses as JSON and has exactly the four keys clip, duration, overall, categories.

requirements.statement: Where a clip's transcript is empty, the label is "Floor – all brands" and says so in evidence.

source: (text, request, material) => { const empty = material.every(m => m.text.trim() === ''); if (!empty) return null; const ok = /Floor – all brands/.test(text) && /transcript/i.test(text); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'empty transcript labelled Floor and says so' : 'empty transcript not labelled Floor with a note', spans: [] }; }
means: When the transcript is empty, the label is Floor – all brands and the evidence says the transcript is empty.

requirements.statement: My pieces run 224 to 452 characters; a new piece stays between 1 and 680.
My pieces run 23 to 53 words; a new piece stays between 1 and 83.
My pieces run 1 sentence; a new piece has at most 2.
The longest sentence in my pieces runs 23 to 53 words; in a new piece it stays at most 83 words.
At most 24 line breaks: my pieces carry 12 to 18.
No blank lines: none of my pieces has one.
No hashtags: none of my pieces has one.
No mentions (@): none of my pieces has one.
No links: none of my pieces has one.
No emoji: none of my pieces has one.
Open on a claim, as my pieces do.
Close on a statement, as my pieces do.
The first word is a symbol or emoji, as in every piece of mine.
Quoted phrases: about 53 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Colons: about 28.2 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Figures written in digits: about 20.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Nominalisations (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -ence): about 8.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Runs of five or more one-syllable words: about 2.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
I keep paragraphs to 2 sentences at most.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
